Why This Is Asked
This checks ability to derive a non-trivial tree DP with knapsack merging over children, handling exact k paths and reconstruction.

- Tree DP on rooted graphs
- Knapsack merge across multiple children

- Complexity considerations

```javascript
function dfs(v, p) { dp[v] = Array(K+1).fill(-INF); dp[v][0] = 0; for (const u of adj[v]) if (u !== p) { dfs(u, v); /* merge dp[v] and dp[u] */ } }
```

- How to reconstruct endpoints efficiently?

## Why This Is Asked
Explores a fresh DP angle: exact partition into k segments with a segment cost defined by range, forcing precomputation and backtracking to recover segment boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Range-based segment cost (max-min)
- Exact partition DP: dp[i][t]
- Precomputation of cost[l][r]
- Backtracking reconstruction

## Code Example
```javascript
// pseudocode for core DP (not complete):
for i in 1..n:
  dp[i][1] = cost[1][i]
for t in 2..k:
  for i in t..n:
    dp[i][t] = min_{l=t-1..i-1} dp[l][t-1] + cost[l+1][i]
    par[i][t] = argmin
```

## Follow-up Questions
- Can you optimize to O(nk) with divide-and-conquer if cost satisfies quadrangle inequality?
- How would you adapt for 0/1-based indexing and streaming inputs?
